I believe in free speech and the importance of hearing different perspectives, even if I strongly disagree with those views. At the same time, I would expect institutions to address any harmful behavior or misinformation in a responsible way.

questions.question: Do you agree or disagree that people like you and your family have a good chance of improving your standard of living in America?
questions.answer: I strongly disagree that people like me and my family have a good chance of improving our standard of living in America right now. With the rising costs of housing and basic necessities in New York, it feels like no matter how hard I work, it’s almost impossible to get ahead. The system seems stacked against people like me who don’t come from wealth, and I worry that without major changes, things will only get harder.

questions.question: How much confidence do you have in the people running the U.S. Supreme Court: a great deal, only some, or hardly any?
questions.answer: I have hardly any confidence in the people running the U.S. Supreme Court. From what I follow in the news, it seems like their decisions often reflect political agendas rather than justice or fairness. It’s really disappointing to see how much influence politics has over what should be an impartial institution. I wish the Court would prioritize the rights and well-being of everyday people instead of catering to powerful interests.

questions.question: If someone in your community wrote a book against churches and religion, would you support removing that book from the library or not?
questions.answer: I would not support removing the book from the library. Even if I don’t agree with the author’s views against churches and religion, I believe in protecting free speech and allowing people to access a wide range of perspectives. Libraries should be spaces for open dialogue and learning, not places where ideas get censored just because they’re controversial. Everyone deserves the chance to decide for themselves what to read and believe.

Diversity is what makes conversations richer and helps us learn from each other. Trying to fit everyone into one mold just feels limiting to me.

questions.question: Do you think we are spending too much, about the right amount, or too little on improving and protecting the nation's health?
questions.answer: I definitely think we’re spending too little on improving and protecting the nation’s health. Especially living in a big city like New York, I see how important accessible healthcare and public health initiatives are. With all the challenges we face, from pandemics to mental health crises, I believe more investment is crucial to make sure everyone gets the care and support they need. It feels like we’re just scratching the surface right now.
